references.text: Jesus's self-identification as 'the light of the world' in John 8:12 corresponds directly with the expression 'the light of the world' in John 11:9, where the light is the condition that one does not stumble.
In John 9:5 Jesus repeats the motif of being 'the light of the world' while he is in the world, which establishes the same theological context for walking in the light as in 11:9.
The warning to 'walk while you have the light' so that darkness does not overtake you mirrors the logic in 11:9 that the light of day prevents stumbling.
Jesus describes himself as the light coming into the world so that no one who believes will remain in darkness, a direct parallel to the function of the light in 11:9.
Paul urges believers to 'walk as children of light' and put aside the deeds of darkness, an ethical application of the same image Jesus uses in 11:9 about walking safely in the light.
